title: HubSpot Pipelines API V1 Rescue
one_liner: Fixed-scope migration sprint for agencies and SaaS products whose HubSpot integrations still call Pipelines API V1 before its 2026-12-04 shutdown.
buyer: HubSpot agencies, RevOps consultancies, SaaS vendors and internal teams with custom scripts or integrations that read or write deal, ticket or custom-object pipeline configuration through the legacy Pipelines API.

pain.description: HubSpot will permanently retire Pipelines API V1 on 2026-12-04. Calls using the old endpoints will stop working. This can break deal/ticket routing, provisioning, reporting or configuration sync in custom integrations. The replacement API changes paths and response structure, so migration requires code and regression testing rather than a simple URL substitution.

observable_targeting.method: Public code repositories, integration documentation and agency-maintained scripts can be scanned for legacy HubSpot pipeline endpoint strings and older HubSpot client patterns before outreach.
observations: HubSpot explicitly recommends auditing codebases for Pipelines V1 calls before the deadline.
Public repositories and wrappers still expose old HubSpot authentication and legacy API usage patterns, showing that obsolete integrations remain discoverable in code.
The acquisition path can therefore be code-first: detect legacy endpoint -> verify active commercial project -> contact only plausible buyers.
Agency portfolios are especially attractive because one relationship can expose multiple affected client integrations.

findings: HubSpot documentation and community posts provide migration guidance for free, so information alone has no value.
HubSpot agencies already advertise audits and migration assistance, confirming a paid service market but also creating competition.
No dominant low-cost fixed-scope code migration offer surfaced in this pass; the opportunity is likely strongest as a rapid implementation sprint or white-label service for agencies.
competitive_validation.risk: The deadline is still several months away and many integrations may already use newer APIs. A generic landing page without prequalified targets would probably waste effort.

offer.name: HubSpot Pipeline API Rescue Sprint
scope: Scan repository/integration code for legacy pipeline calls
Map each affected call to the current HubSpot pipeline API
Regression-test pipeline reads/writes and downstream parsing
Document remaining portal-specific risks and cutover checklist
offer.pricing_note: Quote after code review. Do not promise fixes for unrelated HubSpot workflows, third-party connector internals or portal configuration outside the migration scope.

validation.next_test: Find 10-20 active commercial repositories, agencies or SaaS products with credible evidence of Pipelines V1 use, prioritizing agencies with multiple HubSpot clients; look for at least one explicit paid-interest signal before building a landing page.
validation.promotion_gate: At least one credible buyer requests a code review, migration quote or implementation discussion.

decision.reason: Hard shutdown date, commercially meaningful failure mode and a plausible code-first acquisition channel make this worth validating, but competition and uncertain prevalence argue against building before target discovery.
